races.title: State Senate, District 16
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Gale Adcock
cands.bio: Family nurse practitioner since 1987 and Chief Health Officer at SAS Institute until 2020. Served on the Cary Town Council 2007–2014 and in the NC House (District 41) 2015–2022, including one term as Deputy House Minority Leader. Has represented Senate District 16 since 2023.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed by Ballotpedia among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Adcock on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and teacher pay. Her birthplace is not stated in the pages we read. Her campaign site states positions in general terms only, and she did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. We found no controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond the one listed.

local.label: Roots 55: Adcock was raised in southwestern Virginia and says she has lived in North Carolina since 1976, about 50 years, having arrived as an adult for college.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Eight years in the NC House (2015–2022), including a term as Deputy House Minority Leader, and sitting state senator since 2023 with seats on the Senate Finance and Appropriations (Health and Human Services) committees. Earlier, seven years on the Cary Town Council. Career as a nurse practitioner and SAS Chief Health Officer.
qual.why: Prior legislative service at the state level, plus chamber leadership as Deputy Minority Leader and local elected office, fits the law-and-budget job. The nurse practitioner and health-officer career adds health-policy experience.
qual.label: Prior legislative service at the state level, plus chamber leadership as Deputy Minority Leader and local elected office, fits the law-and-budget job. The nurse practitioner and health-officer career adds health-policy experience.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says she supports conservation tax credits and adequate funding of the Clean Water Management Trust Fund and the Parks and Recreation Trust Fund, and says preserving open space protects water and rural heritage.

cands.name: Philip Hensley
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 16 in 2026. He was also the Republican nominee for North Carolina House District 11 in 2024. Ballotpedia lists no other biographical details.
cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Philip Hensley was born or raised, when he came to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and we found no campaign-site statements, interviews or questionnaires. As a result there are no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or campaign money. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in either race. He has held no elected office, so there is no legislative record to report.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation or work history was found. The only record is two unsuccessful runs for the legislature, in 2024 for House District 11 and in 2026 for Senate District 16.
